scenario.title: Defect Issue Triage and Risk Reporting
scenario.initial_description: When a defect occurs, the engineer reports it, discusses it with related teams, performs additional experiments, and decides how to improve the issue and communicate the risk.

reference_workflow.goal: Triage a defect issue, coordinate investigation, and report improvement actions and customer risk.

activities.name: Register defect issue with initial evidence
Classify issue severity and affected scope
Notify related teams and assign owners
Review experiment result and select improvement action
Share final report and action items

decisions.condition: Does the experiment support the root-cause hypothesis?

automation_opportunities.rationale: Issue reports can be pre-structured from defect descriptions and evidence attachments.
Related teams can be suggested from issue category and affected process area.
Action-item extraction and risk report drafting can be partially automated.

activities.name: Cross-Team Triage Discussion
activities.actor: Engineer, Quality Team, Development Team, Operations Team

activities.name: Additional Experimentation and Root Cause Analysis

decisions.condition: Is the defect reproducible and sufficiently documented after initial logging?
branches: Yes: Proceed to Cross-Team Triage Discussion (A3)
No: Return to Engineer for additional information gathering (A1)

decisions.condition: Is the severity classification Critical or High?
branches: Yes: Expedite to Additional Experimentation (A5) with elevated priority

decisions.condition: Is the root cause confirmed after experimentation?
branches: Yes: Proceed to Improvement Action Planning (A7)
No: Return to Additional Experimentation (A5) with revised hypothesis

decisions.condition: Does the risk score exceed the escalation threshold?
branches: No: Proceed directly to Risk Communication (A10)

decisions.condition: Does verification confirm the defect is resolved?
branches: No: Re-open defect and return to Improvement Action Planning (A7)

exceptions: Defect cannot be reproduced: Loop back to data collection with expanded scope
Key team member unavailable for triage: Designate alternate representative or delay triage with documented justification
Experimentation resources unavailable: Escalate resource conflict to management before proceeding
Root cause remains ambiguous after multiple experiment cycles: Escalate to external expert review
Regulatory or compliance defect detected: Immediately trigger mandatory reporting process outside standard workflow
Corrective action introduces new defects: Re-initiate defect report for secondary defect
Stakeholder communication fails or is rejected: Log failed communication and retry with alternate channel

automation_opportunities.target: A1 - Defect Detection and Initial Logging
automation_opportunities.rationale: Automated defect detection through monitoring systems, sensor data, or test pipelines can pre-populate defect report fields, reducing manual data entry and time-to-report. Anomaly detection algorithms can flag defects before an engineer manually identifies them.
constraints: Requires integration with monitoring or test infrastructure
False positive rate must be controlled to avoid alert fatigue
Data quality and completeness of automated signals must be validated

automation_opportunities.rationale: Automated form validation, mandatory field enforcement, and auto-routing of notifications to relevant teams upon submission can eliminate manual coordination overhead and reduce submission errors.
constraints: Routing logic must be maintained as team structures change
Some defect types may require manual nuance in description that automation cannot capture

automation_opportunities.rationale: A rule-based or machine learning classification model trained on historical defect records can automatically assign initial severity and priority scores, enabling faster triage and reducing subjective inconsistency.
required_data: Historical defect records with severity labels
constraints: Model must be auditable for regulated environments
Human review gate should remain for critical or novel defect types
Training data must be representative and unbiased

automation_opportunities.target: D1 - Is the defect reproducible and sufficiently documented?
automation_opportunities.rationale: Automated completeness checks on the defect report fields and cross-referencing with system logs to assess reproducibility signals can programmatically determine if a report is ready for triage, reducing manual back-and-forth.
constraints: Reproducibility may depend on environmental conditions that are not fully machine-readable
Edge cases with ambiguous documentation may still require human judgment

automation_opportunities.target: A5 - Additional Experimentation and Root Cause Analysis
automation_opportunities.rationale: Automated experiment scheduling, data collection, and preliminary statistical analysis can accelerate root cause investigation. Workflow orchestration tools can assign experiment tasks and aggregate results without manual coordination.
constraints: Physical or laboratory experiments may not be fully automatable
Domain-specific knowledge is often required to design meaningful experiments
Experiment infrastructure integration may be complex

automation_opportunities.target: A8 - Risk Assessment and Impact Evaluation
automation_opportunities.rationale: Standardized risk scoring models can be automated using defect severity, scope, and corrective action data as inputs, producing consistent and reproducible risk scores and draft reports without manual calculation.
constraints: Risk models must be reviewed and approved by risk officers before automation
Novel defect categories may fall outside model scope
Regulatory requirements may mandate human sign-off on risk scores

automation_opportunities.target: D4 - Does the risk score exceed the escalation threshold?
automation_opportunities.rationale: Threshold-based decision logic can be fully automated: if the computed risk score exceeds a defined threshold, the system automatically routes to the escalation activity and notifies the Risk Officer, eliminating manual decision overhead.
constraints: Thresholds must be formally defined and periodically reviewed
Audit trail of automated escalation decisions must be maintained
Override mechanism must exist for edge cases

automation_opportunities.target: A10 - Risk Communication and Stakeholder Reporting
automation_opportunities.rationale: Report generation and distribution can be automated using templates populated with risk assessment outputs, with automated delivery to a pre-configured stakeholder list and communication logging upon confirmation of receipt.
constraints: Sensitive risk content may require human review before distribution
Stakeholder list must be kept current
Regulatory reporting formats may impose specific structure requirements

automation_opportunities.rationale: Automated regression testing or verification test suites can be triggered post-implementation to confirm defect resolution, with results automatically compared against closure criteria and defect records updated accordingly.
constraints: Not all defect types have automatable verification tests
Physical or process-level changes may require manual inspection
Test environment must mirror production conditions for results to be valid

assumptions: A defect tracking system exists and is accessible to all relevant actors throughout the workflow.
Cross-team triage discussions occur in synchronous or asynchronous collaborative sessions, not solely via email chains.
Severity classification criteria and risk scoring rubrics are formally defined but may not yet be digitally encoded.
Additional experimentation may involve both computational and physical or laboratory activities depending on the defect domain.
Escalation thresholds for risk scores exist in policy but may require formalization before automation can be applied.
Stakeholder lists for risk communication are maintained in an accessible registry.
Historical defect records with labeled outcomes are available to support potential machine learning applications.
Regulatory or compliance constraints may apply to certain defect categories and would trigger parallel mandatory reporting processes not detailed in the base workflow.
Defect closure requires both technical verification and quality team sign-off, not verification alone.
The workflow described applies to a single defect instance; batch or systemic defects affecting multiple records may require workflow extensions.

missing_information.gap: Roles involved in defect triage are not defined beyond 'engineer' and 'related teams'
missing_information.why_it_matters: Without knowing which specific roles (e.g., quality engineer, product owner, safety officer, management) participate at each step, it is impossible to map handoffs, assign automation targets, or identify bottlenecks caused by human dependencies.

missing_information.gap: No systems or tools are mentioned for defect reporting, tracking, or communication
missing_information.why_it_matters: Automation assessment requires knowing whether a defect tracking system, ticketing platform, or communication tool exists, as these determine integration feasibility and data availability.

missing_information.gap: The format and source of the initial defect report are unspecified
missing_information.why_it_matters: Structured vs. unstructured defect reports drastically affect whether automated intake, classification, or routing is feasible.

missing_information.gap: No decision criteria are defined for triage outcomes (e.g., severity levels, risk thresholds, escalation rules)
missing_information.why_it_matters: Without explicit decision logic, it is not possible to assess whether triage decisions can be automated or supported by rule-based or ML-based systems.

missing_information.gap: The format and recipients of the risk communication output are not described
missing_information.why_it_matters: The structure of risk reports and their distribution channels determine whether report generation and dissemination can be automated.

missing_information.gap: Volume and frequency of defect occurrences are unknown
missing_information.why_it_matters: Automation ROI depends heavily on how often this process runs; a rare process may not justify automation investment.

missing_information.gap: Time spent on each step (reporting, discussion, experiments, improvement planning, risk communication) is not quantified
missing_information.why_it_matters: Without effort estimates per activity, it is impossible to prioritize which steps offer the greatest automation benefit.

missing_information.gap: No exception or escalation paths are described (e.g., critical safety defects, unresolved disagreements between teams)
missing_information.why_it_matters: Exception handling is often where process failures occur and where automation guardrails are most needed; omitting it leads to incomplete workflow models.

missing_information.gap: Dependencies between the discussion step and the experiment step are unclear (e.g., must discussion conclude before experiments begin?)
missing_information.why_it_matters: Sequential vs. parallel activity structure affects process cycle time and the feasibility of workflow orchestration automation.

missing_information.gap: No approval gates or sign-off requirements are mentioned before risk is communicated externally
missing_information.why_it_matters: If regulatory, legal, or management approvals are required before risk reporting, these must be modeled as control points, which affects automation scope.

missing_information.gap: It is unclear whether historical defect data exists in a structured, queryable format
missing_information.why_it_matters: Process mining and ML-based automation require historical event logs; absence of structured data may block both analysis and automation.

missing_information.gap: No information is provided about whether teams involved operate in separate systems or organizational units
missing_information.why_it_matters: Cross-system or cross-organizational collaboration introduces integration constraints that may limit automation to notification or orchestration rather than full end-to-end automation.

clarification_questions.question: Who are the specific roles involved at each step of the triage process (defect reporting, team discussion, experimentation, improvement decision, and risk communication), and is there a designated decision-maker for escalations?
What systems or tools are currently used to log defects, manage discussions, track experiments, and distribute risk reports (e.g., ticketing systems, collaboration platforms, document repositories)?
What criteria determine the severity or risk level of a defect, and are there defined thresholds that trigger different triage paths or escalation procedures?

How frequently do defects occur that trigger this full triage workflow, and approximately how much time does each step (reporting, discussion, experiments, improvement planning, risk communication) take on average?
Is any approval or sign-off required before a risk report is communicated externally or to management, and if so, who must approve it and under what conditions?
Are historical defect records stored in a structured format with timestamps and status changes that could serve as an event log for process mining analysis?
